lines: Home with no one missing. That's the whole job, really.
Home again, whole enough to thank you properly. That matters.
We came back with the village still ahead of us. I'll count that as good work.
I was not sure about leaving. Coming back safely makes the choice easier to carry.
The road was long, but you kept your word about getting me home.
My bed has never looked so inviting.
I checked the flock before I even put my pack down.
No wounds, no lost supplies, and no one left behind. I will take that result.
You chose the careful route when the quick one turned dangerous.
I expected trouble. I did not expect you to handle it that calmly.
The village bell sounded good after so many strange miles.
We worked well together once we learned each other's pace.
I came home with better boots and a better opinion of you.
The journey gave me stories without giving me scars.
You watched the road while I watched the weather. It worked.
I would travel with you again, though I would pack more food.
The flock recognized me before half the villagers did.
Nothing followed us home. I checked twice.
Thank you for treating my safety like part of the plan.
We left as strangers. I do not think we returned that way.
I am back in the fold, but I was not guarded as carefully as I hoped.
I made it home, but the road took more from me than it should have.
Next time, let us return with fewer marks and better choices.
This cut will close. My questions about that route may take longer.
You kept moving after I asked for rest. I paid for that decision.
I can walk, but I will not pretend the journey went well.
The healer says I was lucky. I would rather have been protected.
I followed your lead and ended up under a falling blade.
My ribs hurt every time someone calls the trip a success.
You got me home. You also got me hurt.
I needed a shield beside me, not ten steps ahead.
The wound is clean now. The memory is not.
I should have spoken sooner when the pace became unsafe.
We survived because we turned back, not because the plan was sound.
I will need time before I agree to another road with you.
At least the flock does not ask why I am limping.
You apologized at the gate. I heard you. I am still angry.
The supplies made it back in better condition than I did.
Next time, listen when the person behind you says stop.
I am grateful to be home and disappointed in how we arrived.
A shepherd who strikes the flock earns no easy trust.
Following you was trust. What happened after was something else.
A guide who strikes from close by leaves the longest mark.
I watched the road for danger. I should have watched you.
You asked me to follow, then made me regret saying yes.
Do not call it an accident when you never warned me.
The bruise will fade before the betrayal does.
I thought we were on the same side until you raised your weapon.
You knew I trusted you. That is what makes it worse.
I will not travel alone with you again.
Stay away from the flock until I decide what to tell the others.
You cannot lead someone and treat them like a target.
I remember the look on your face more clearly than the blow.
If you want forgiveness, start with the truth.
I came home wondering whether any part of your offer was honest.
Do not ask me to make this easier for you.
I should not have to fear the person who promised safe passage.
You left me choosing between the road and the one guiding me.
The village will hear what happened from me.
Trust is not wool. I cannot simply mend the torn part.
Keeping me in the boat was the hard part. I have chased calmer sheep.
The boat did its part. I am still deciding whether the rest of the plan did.
<aqua><wavy>Water</wavy></aqua> carried us home, which is more than I expected from that journey.
I kissed the dock when we landed. Quietly, so no one could enjoy it.
You said the crossing would save time. It certainly gave me time to worry.
My legs still feel the river moving under them.
The boat leaked less than I feared and more than I liked.
I kept our supplies dry while you argued with the current.
We nearly lost an oar, then nearly lost our tempers.
I would have preferred a road, even a bad one.
The far shore looked close for an unreasonable amount of time.
You steered us around the rocks well enough. I noticed.
I did not know a sheep bell could sound comforting from that far away.
We reached home before the rain, which may be the best thing I can say.
Next time, give me warning before pushing away from shore.
The fish seemed calm. I resented them for it.
You handled the rough water better than I expected.
I spent the last half of the trip planning my first step onto land.
Nothing fell overboard, though several things considered it.
I am home, dry, and not getting into another boat today.
